question: Lipids are transferred from intestine to liver by
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Lipids absorbed in intestine" -> "Chylomicrons formed in intestinal cells" -> "Chylomicrons enter lymphatic system" -> "Chylomicrons transported to bloodstream" -> "Chylomicrons deliver lipids to liver" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Dietary fats ingested" -> "Intestinal mucosa processes fats" -> "Chylomicrons released into circulation" -> "Chylomicrons carry lipids to liver" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Lipids from food" -> "Intestinal absorption" -> "Formation of chylomicrons" -> "Chylomicrons transport lipids to liver" -> 92%
CHAIN: "Lipids enter bloodstream" -> "Chylomicrons transport lipids" -> "Chylomicrons deliver to liver" -> 93%
analysis: Lipids absorbed from the intestine are primarily transported to the liver in the form of chylomicrons. These are lipoprotein particles that carry dietary lipids from the intestines to other locations in the body, including the liver.
